visual_action: The video starts with grainy, black-and-white historical footage of a protest march for reproductive rights. It then cuts to modern, full-color footage of a large contemporary protest march on a city street in front of a large government-style building. Protesters in the modern clip hold signs with slogans like "BANS OFF OUR BODIES" and "LIBERATE ABORTION".

cast.name: American supporters of reproductive rights
cast.evidence: The on-screen text explicitly names "Generations of Americans" and "the majority of Americans who support Roe v. Wade". The visuals show crowds of these supporters protesting.

on_screen_text.text: Generations of Americans fought for reproductive rights...
and so are the majority of Americans who support Roe v. Wade

spoken_summary: There is no spoken dialogue in the video. The audio consists of a sigh at the beginning followed by a song.
audio_music: The video begins with the sound of a person sighing, suggesting weariness. This is immediately followed by a drum intro that leads into a slow, atmospheric, and somewhat somber indie rock song that plays for the remainder of the clip. The music creates a determined and reflective mood. The track is identified as "Apocalypse" by Cigarettes After Sex.
editing_pacing: The editing is simple and slow-paced, consisting of two long clips—one historical and one modern—joined by a single cut. It functions like a slideshow.
emotions_signaled: Solidarity (shown through visuals of historical and contemporary protest marches)
cultural_references: The song "Apocalypse" by Cigarettes After Sex is used as the soundtrack.
central_claim: A majority of Americans support reproductive rights (specifically Roe v. Wade), continuing a multi-generational fight for the cause.
intended_effect: To inspire solidarity and action in support of reproductive rights by framing it as a historically significant and popular majority movement.
